label: Observed Context Label Does Not Bound a Hidden Fiber
statement: If q(a)=q(b) and only actual context a is tested with e(a)=0, the compatible models e0(a)=e0(b)=0 and e1(a)=0,e1(b)=M agree on the observed label and tested law but differ maximally at b. Partial observation alone therefore yields no nontrivial hidden-fiber amplitude bound.
domain: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
scope: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
source_lineage: Elementary partial-identification counterexample specialized to R167 hidden redundancy.
proof: Direct construction; observed/tested objects are equal while hidden maxima are zero and M.
counterexamples_and_limits: A physically certified within-fiber regularity/lift premise can add a bound; the counterexample denies inference without it.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one coarse observation fiber with two actual hidden contexts
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: there exist two compatible models with maximal hidden-effect separation
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same observed label is not identity of actual physical context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Block observed-label equality from masquerading as route closure

label: Envelope Evidence Does Not Identify d and L Separately
statement: For every c>0, d'=c d and L'=L/c leave every Ld product and the full R168 cone envelope unchanged; envelope data therefore do not separately identify metric scale and Lipschitz constant, while route budgets record their operational product directly in d_F units.
domain: Any R168 metric-envelope application and positive scalar rescaling.
scope: Any R168 metric-envelope application and positive scalar rescaling.
source_lineage: Elementary scale invariance applied to R168's metric envelope.
proof: (L/c)(c d)=Ld pointwise; all cone terms and their infimum/cap are unchanged.
counterexamples_and_limits: A unit convention can choose one representative but adds no physical evidence; the discriminator class F remains scientifically substantive.

formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: representation-level statement; no new actual bearer inferred
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Prevent a small reported L from masquerading as stronger evidence

label: Valid Held-Out Lower Evidence Can Refute an Edge or Path Budget
statement: If an independently challenged actual edge/path has a valid consumer-law lower bound larger than its declared upper budget, the calibration certificate is refuted; this is distinct from a valid mediator-effect envelope refuting effects above tau.
domain: One frozen route certificate and an independent actual challenge under the same K0/F/consumer/time contract.
scope: One frozen route certificate and an independent actual challenge under the same K0/F/consumer/time contract.
source_lineage: Prospective falsification discipline from R161-R168, applied to local route upper budgets.
proof: A simultaneously valid lower bound above a claimed upper bound makes the certificate conjunction false.
counterexamples_and_limits: Invalid challenge delivery or a post-hoc discriminator cannot refute the certificate; passing finitely many challenges does not prove omitted-route completeness.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: one frozen local/path upper certificate and independent lower-bound challenge
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: existential valid violation refutes the certificate; no converse completeness inference
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same actual route variables, consumer and pre-compensation timing
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Make physical calibration rejectable rather than decorative
